instructions: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water, bring it to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until the chicken is ready.
Pat the chicken dry and cut it into 3/4-inch pieces. Transfer it to a bowl and toss with 3/4 tsp of the salt, 1/2 tsp of the black pepper and 3/4 tsp of the five spice. Leave it for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the onion and bell pepper into 1/2-inch pieces, mince the garlic and slice the green onions. Slice the cucumber. In a small bowl, mix the remaining 3/4 tsp salt, the remaining 1/4 tsp black pepper, the remaining 1/2 tsp five spice and the sugar. Put the cornstarch on a plate.
Dredge the chicken in the cornstarch in batches, shaking off the extra.
Heat the oil in a large heavy skillet or wok over medium-high heat for about 3 minutes. It's ready when a pinch of cornstarch sizzles right away.

Fry half the chicken in a single layer for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden. Transfer it to a plate lined with paper towels. Repeat with the rest. You're cooking it to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Pour the oil into a heatproof bowl, leaving 1 tbsp in the pan. Let the bowl cool before you discard the oil.
Return the pan to medium-high heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and toss for 1 minute. Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the chicken and sprinkle in the seasoning mix. Toss for 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice and the sliced cucumber.
method_notes: No version read had a rating, so the lead is the best-read real version of the dish: The Koole Mom's boneless chicken thighs marinated in salt, pepper and five spice, dredged in cornstarch, fried, then tossed with onion, bell pepper, garlic and green onion and a salt, pepper and five spice finish. Vicky Pham's wing version (5.0 from 1 rating) agrees on frying then tossing with garlic, shallot and green onion in a seasoned salt, and adds the pinch of sugar in the salt and pepper mix. That is where the salty-sweet in the list's line comes from; the dish is mostly salty and peppery. The lead fries twice and deep fries in a cup of oil. Here the chicken is cut small and fried once to stay near 30 minutes. Shaoxing wine, MSG and chicken powder are left out to keep it gluten-free, and jalapeno is left off to keep the base mild.
